title: Post Optimize config-change alerts with rollback links + correlation IDs
author: Devon Price
description:
Context: As part of the Safe apply + rollback mechanism, on-call needs config-change visibility directly in incident channels, plus a reliable way to jump to a rollback action when a rollout is suspected to be the cause. This PR teaches incident-bot to (1) listen for Optimize config apply/rollback events emitted by the control plane, (2) post a structured Slack message to the target incident channel(s) with the scope + version + correlation id, and (3) include a deep link to the Console compare view and rollback flow for the affected scope/version. It also captures the correlation id in the incident channel topic (when permitted) to make log/trace pivoting easier during active mitigation.

What’s included: - New event handler for `optimize.config.apply_*` and `optimize.config.rollback_*` event types (attempted/applied/failed + attempted/rolled_back/failed). - Slack blocks formatting with a short, scannable summary (customer/tenant, deployment mode, region/cluster, route/model) and a compact “diff hint” (changed fields count only; no values). - “Rollback” CTA button that deep-links into Console and pre-fills scope + target version; button is only shown for events where rollback is applicable (apply_applied / apply_failed with version) and when we have enough scope fields to generate a stable URL. - Correlation id propagation: incident-bot now threads the `correlation_id` from the event payload into the posted message (and into the incident channel topic when the channel is tagged as `#inc-*` and topic updates are enabled). - Redaction rules: we do not include prompt/customer content; config values are not shown, only field names and counts. Request IDs are truncated to 8 chars in the visible message with the full id in a hidden context block.

Out of scope: - No automated rollback trigger. - No attempt to compute diffs inside incident-bot; we rely on control plane diff summary fields and Console compare view.

Example Slack output (sanitized): Optimize config change detected: `apply_applied` • scope: tenant=helixbank-prod / mode=Dedicated / region=us-east-1 / route=/v1/chat/completions / model=rw-llama-70b • version: v42 (from v41) • correlation: `cfgchg_9f2a18c3` • changed fields: 3 • Actions: [View history] [Compare] [Rollback to v41]

Flags / rollout: - Feature-gated behind `INCIDENT_BOT_OPTIMIZE_CONFIG_ALERTS` (default off). - Per-workspace allowlist via `optimize_config_alert_workspaces` to avoid spamming non-prod channels.

Why now: This addresses repeated feedback from SRE + enterprise customers that auditability and rollback need to be operable under incident pressure (ref SUP-2423 and incident thread 1731349988).
commits: incident-bot: add Optimize config change event models + validation
incident-bot: Slack blocks for config apply/rollback notifications
incident-bot: add Console deep links (history/compare/rollback) + scope normalization
incident-bot: store/post correlation_id + topic update plumbing
incident-bot: tests (unit + golden Slack payload snapshots) and docs
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we guarantee we always have a correlation id? If missing, I’d rather not post a blank field. Also please ensure we don’t log full request ids to stdout (PII-ish).

Devon Price (author): Updated handler to treat correlation_id as optional. If missing we omit the line entirely and we do not update the channel topic. Also changed logging to only emit `request_id_prefix` (first 8 chars) and added a unit test for redaction.
Rafael Mendes (review): Rollback link: can we default to ‘rollback to previous known-good’ instead of ‘rollback to N-1’? In incidents people will click quickly and we should avoid ambiguous behavior.

Devon Price (author): Agree. The link now targets the `previous_version_id` provided by control plane when present. If not present we render only History/Compare (no Rollback). Added a note in description and tests for both cases.
Chloe Martin (review): Please align event type names with control plane: I think we standardized on `optimize.config.apply_applied` etc (dot-separated). Your initial commit used underscores.
Devon Price (author): Fixed to dot-separated strings and updated the router. Also added schema validation to fail closed (unknown events are dropped with a metric).
Svetlana Petrenko (review): For enterprises, some workspaces require external URL allowlisting. Can we add a config option to use a custom Console base URL (Private deployments)?
Devon Price (author): Added `console_base_url` per workspace (defaults to https://console.redwoodinference.com). The URL builder now reads from workspace config. Documented in README.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Looks good. The message is concise and the rollback CTA is exactly what on-call asked for. Approving once CI is green.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved with the redaction + optional correlation id changes.
qa_notes: Validated in staging workspace `#inc-staging-sre`: emitted synthetic `optimize.config.apply_applied` event with scope (Dedicated/us-east-1) and verified Slack message, buttons, and topic update. Verified feature flag disabled results in no message. Verified Private Console base URL override renders correct deep links without trailing slashes.
release_notes: incident-bot now posts Optimize config apply/rollback events to incident channels (feature-flagged), including correlation ids and Console deep links (history/compare/rollback).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge by Devon Price after approvals; feature flag remains OFF by default and will be enabled per-workspace during internal beta.
